properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following river in Florida...

For the Shoal River...including Crestview...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on
the Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.

The next statement will be issued when updates occur.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Shoal River near Crestview.

* WHEN...From early this morning to Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, homes on south bank of river begin to flood
near Crestview. At 15.0 feet, water in Trevor Court. Some homes in

this morning to a crest of 14.9 feet tomorrow evening. It will
then fall below flood stage Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.8
feet on 07/08/1994.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Elba, Enterprise, Fort Rucker, New Brockton, Lee, Woodland Grove
Church, Camp Humming Hills, Richburg, Wise Mill, Arcus, Mixons
Crossroads, Clintonville, Lowry Mill, Carl Folsom A/p, Tabernacle,
New Haven, Turner Crossroads, Victoria, Camp Alaflo Bsa and Jack.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.areaDesc: Ashe; Alleghany; Surry; Watauga; Wilkes; Grayson; Carroll; Floyd; Patrick
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 1:24AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of North Carolina, including the following areas,
Alleghany NC, Ashe, Surry, Watauga and Wilkes and southwest
Virginia, including the following areas, Carroll, Floyd, Grayson
and Patrick.

* WHEN...From 11 AM EDT this morning through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with
debris. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers
are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Upslope rainfall from a rather strong southeasterly Low level jet
from the remnants of Isaias will bring increased precipitation
along the crest of the southern Blue Ridge from Floyd county
extending southwestward to Watauga county. Widespread rainfall
totals of 2-4 inches with locally higher totals in the 5-6 range
will be possible, especially for areas like Meadows of Dan,
Boone, and Blowing Rock. These higher totals may lead to isolated
instances of landslides along slopes that have been modified by
humans like embankments or cut slopes. These areas may also see
increased rises on local streamflows that may lead to flooding
across low-water crossings.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...In North Carolina, Ashe and Watauga Counties. In Virginia,
Grayson, Smyth, and Tazewell Counties. In West Virginia, Mercer,
Summers, and Western Greenbrier Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 11 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strong easterly to southeasterly winds from
the remnants of Isaias will move over the region today into Sunday,
which may lead to downed trees and power poles and subsequently
power outages across higher terrain locations from NW North
Carolina to SE West Virginia.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 9 at 10:09PM PDT until October 10 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 274 Southern Mono County, 420
Northern Sierra Front including Carson City, Douglas, Storey,
Southern Washoe, Western Lyon, and Far Southern Lassen Counties,
421 Southern Sierra Front including Alpine, Northern Mono, Southern
Lyon, and Western Mineral Counties, 423 West Humboldt Basin in
Pershing County, and 429 Lahontan Basin including Churchill and
Eastern Mineral Counties.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 9 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts 35 to 45 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimum Humidity between 14 to 22 percent.

* DURATION...3 to 6 hours.

* IMPACTS...The combination of gusty winds and prolonged dry
conditions, even in areas where humidity may not be as low, can
cause fires to rapidly grow in size and intensity before first
responders can contain them.
properties.instruction:
Avoid outdoor activities that can cause a spark near dry vegetation,
such as yard work, target shooting, or campfires. Follow local fire
restrictions. Check weather.gov/reno for updates and
livingwithfire.info for preparedness tips.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 9 at 10:07PM PDT until October 12 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday afternoon. .

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.
